transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-30 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 min
Attendees: Maya (AE), Connor (SE), Elena (CSM) -- Verdant: Alex (VP Eng), Priya (SRE), Jonah (Procurement), Samira (Data Privacy), Liam (DevOps)

00:00 Maya: okay hi everyone thanks for joining on short notice um this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick off and then pass to Connor for the tech bits. big agenda: renewal term options, eu-edge onboarding, and the small benchmark we promised.
00:18 Alex: yep thanks Maya, quick thing first: procurement wants to understand if we can get a 12 vs 24 month term and what the unit economics look like. we've got a hard go-live in Q4 so timeline tight.
00:30 Maya: understood. we can show 12 and 24 month pricing, also a committed reserved capacity discount for Dedicated. we'll put EU-edge as a separate line item so you're not double charged for burst.
00:45 Jonah: are there any minimums for the EU edge? we prefer a predictable monthly commitment.
00:52 Connor: technically the EU edge is a VPC-attached deployment, it maps to a dedicated pool of instances. minimum is typically a half-node equivalent in our contract terms for the pilot, but we can model monthly commit tiers — Maya will include that. apologies, *half-node equivalent* is an internal shorthand.
01:08 Priya: on the SRE side a few questions: what's the p95 latency we should expect for short prompt workloads (sub-1024 tokens) from EU-edge? and how does prefix caching behave across sessions?
01:22 Connor: good q. in our benchmarks we usually see p95 in the 45–120ms range for small prompt sizes on EU-edge depending on batch strategy and kernel selection. with prefix/KV caching enabled we'll see much lower downstream token costs and improved latency for multi-turn. note: our transcript bench note — sometimes the caching hit rate drops if session affinity isn't pinned, so you want sticky routing.
01:45 Samira: on privacy: the PHI workflows — can we have HSM/KMS integration? and audit log retention? we need at least 3 years of immutable logs for some studies.
01:58 Elena: yep we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and can integrate with HSM-backed keys for encryption in flight/at rest. retention windows are configurable; for hosted we have configurable export to your S3 or secure bucket. we'll surface the SOC2 artifacts and the specifics of export APIs.
02:12 Samira: and what about data residency — if we spin up EU-edge, are all logs and tokens kept inside the EU cluster?
02:20 Connor: yes, EU-edge keeps data in region provided you pin the VPC and disallow cross-region fallbacks. fallback behavior is configurable, we won't cross-region unless you enable a fallback policy, otherwise requests failover to a different model variant within the same region. note: if capacity constrained and you accept degraded model variant the model outputs could differ slightly.
02:38 Alex: okay that fallback detail matters. we cannot have models hitting US infra for PHI.
02:43 Maya: understood. we'll document a no-fallback policy for EU PHI routes in the SOW.
03:00 Priya: for the benchmark: what workload should we give you? we can provide production traffic profile but sanitized.
03:07 Connor: perfect — sample RT logs (anonymized) with request size distributions and concurrency will be ideal. we'll run a 48-hour run to capture diurnal patterns and warm/cold start behaviour. we'll report p50/p95/p99, token-level cost, KV cache hit rates, and memory/kv utilization.
03:30 Liam: how do you handle quantization? our ops folks are eyeing lower precision stacks to save cost but worried about hallucination increases.
03:40 Connor: we support multiple quant profiles; we can recommend Q4/Q8 variants per-model. in my experience q8 gives ~2–3x cost reduction with minimal quality drop for these LLMs but we'll include quality-regression checks in the bench. note: sometimes transcription shows that as *quantizashun* in older notes ha.
04:00 Jonah: procurement question: will the SOW include an explicit SLA for p95 latency and availability for the Dedicated / EU-edge lines?
04:10 Maya: yes SLA language is standard for Dedicated and Private; hosted has SLOs. for Dedicated we can commit to 99.9% SLA and a latency target we measure under specified load — i'll include measurable buckets in the SOW.
04:25 Alex: are there penalties or credits if latency degrades due to kernel regressions on your side?
04:32 Elena: we typically do credits tied to availability; for latency regressions we have rollback and can roll to the verified model variant. we also have regression alerting and a rollback playbook — we'll attach that.
04:45 Samira: security questionnaire — we need to complete a vendor assessment. will you fill out the details around key rotation and audit logs?
04:52 Elena: yes i'll fill out the questionnaire and loop Dr. Samira in. we'll also share the SOC2 report and our pen test summary.
05:05 Priya: on capacity: we want a baseline committed capacity for the app at 1.2k concurrent, with burst up to 2k for 4 hours/day during peak; does that map cleanly?
05:18 Connor: yes that's doable. we have burst pools; we can model guaranteed throughput for 1.2k on reserved nodes and a burst pool for spikes. costs for burst differ slightly — you'll see that in the pricing tiers.
05:30 Alex: timeline — we want EU-edge in production by Nov 15. is that feasible?
05:35 Maya: aggressive but feasible with a pilot in late September. propose: SOW sign by 09/10, pilot provisioning 09/15, 48h bench 09/20–09/22, pilot validation week of 09/27, then staged rollout.
05:51 Jonah: our procurement window for Q4 spend needs signed SOW by 09/10 ideally.
05:55 Maya: we'll aim for that. I'll send updated SOW by end of week with pricing and the no-fallback EU PHI clause.
06:10 Priya: small note — do you support SAML SSO + RBAC on per-route tokens? we want fine-grained access and token scoping for dev vs prod teams.
06:20 Elena: yes SAML SSO for the console, and RBAC for users; token scoping per-route is available and we can set different retention/expunge policies per-token.
06:32 Liam: any gotchas with VPC peering? our network team wants minimal rule changes.
06:38 Connor: we use customer-managed VPC with specific peering subnets; network team will only need to allow egress to the edge endpoint and route the peering, we can provide playbook for firewall rules. sometimes the firewall appliance names get transcribed weird in old notes.
06:50 Alex: okay i think we're aligned. quick recap?
06:54 Maya: sure — action list: i'll send SOW/pricing incl EU edge by 09/03, Elena will push security artifacts and fill questionnaire, Connor will run 48h bench after Priya provides logs, and Jonah will share PO timeline. we'll aim for SOW sign 09/10.
07:10 Jonah: sounds good, i'll follow up internally on PO. thanks all.
07:15 Maya: thank you everyone. we'll schedule the bench kick-off for next Tues 09:00 BST and i'll cc procurement. bye.

Notes: occasional transcription hiccups — speaker overlap around 03:30 and some tech words transcribed oddly (quantizashun, KV cash). Shared links referenced: [SOW template] (link not pasted), [Security packet] (uploaded post-call).
file_notes: Recorded on customer-success workspace; call primarily CSM/AE-led with SE technical input. Customer wants EU-only data residency for PHI routes; no cross-region fallback. Emphasis on SOW timelines and procurement cutoffs.
